title: What If Your Supermarket Banana Went Extinct?

scenes.text: What if bananas went extinct? It has happened to the banana before.
Before the 1960s the world ate a different banana, the Gros Michel. A soil fungus wiped it out.
The Cavendish replaced it. Today it makes up nearly half of all banana production and exports.
Every Cavendish is a clone, so one disease can hit them all. That disease is Tropical Race 4, a strain of the same fungus.
It began in Malaysia around 1990 and has reached Asia, Australia, Africa and the Middle East. Infected soil can't simply be replanted with bananas.
So bananas wouldn't vanish overnight. Hundreds of other kinds exist. But the one in your store could, and it already did once.
